question: Which of the following article of Indian constitution deals with the definition of money bill?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 110**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 110** of the **Indian Constitution** defines a **Money Bill**. It specifies the provisions under which a Bill can be classified as a Money Bill.
 
• A Money Bill includes provisions related to **taxation, borrowing of money by the government, expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, or custody of funds in the Public Account of India**.
 
• A Bill shall be deemed to be a Money Bill only if it deals exclusively with matters listed in Article 110, including **the imposition, abolition, remission, alteration, or regulation of taxes**.
 
• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha has the exclusive authority to decide whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not, and their decision is considered final.
 
• Money Bills can only be introduced in the **Lok Sabha**, not in the Rajya Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha cannot amend or reject a Money Bill. It can only make recommendations, which the Lok Sabha may or may not accept.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Difference Between Money Bill and Financial Bill:**

 
 
• A **Money Bill** is defined under **Article 110** and deals exclusively with matters specified therein. A **Financial Bill**, on the other hand, has provisions related to revenue but does not exclusively deal with matters listed under Article 110.
 
• While a Money Bill can only be introduced in the **Lok Sabha**, Financial Bills can be introduced in either House of Parliament.
 
• The Speaker certifies a Bill as a Money Bill, while Financial Bills do not require such certification.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions for Money Bill:**
 
 
• **Article 109**: Discusses the procedure for passing a Money Bill in Parliament.
 
• **Article 117**: Deals with Financial Bills other than Money Bills.
 
• **Article 112**: Refers to the Annual Financial Statement (Budget), which may include Money Bills.
 
 
 
• **Process of Passing Money Bill:**
 
 
• Introduced only in the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• Once passed by the Lok Sabha, it is sent to the **Rajya Sabha**, which can only make recommendations within 14 days.
 
• The Lok Sabha can accept or reject the recommendations, and the Bill is considered passed even if the Rajya Sabha does not return it within 14 days.
 
• After being passed by both Houses (or only the Lok Sabha effectively), the Bill is sent for the **President's assent**.
 
 
 
• **Important Examples of Money Bills:**
 
 
• The **Goods and Services Tax (GST) Bill** was passed as a Money Bill in 2017.
 
• Other examples include Bills related to income tax amendments, appropriation of funds, and public borrowing.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 110** is crucial for maintaining the separation of powers between the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha regarding financial legislation.
 
• The Speaker's decision on classifying a Bill as a Money Bill is final and cannot be challenged in court.
 
• This provision ensures that financial matters remain under the control of the directly elected representatives of the people in the Lok Sabha.
 
• Money Bills are an integral part of India's parliamentary democracy, where the government requires legislative approval to impose taxes or spend public funds.
 
• Understanding the provisions of Article 110 is essential for comprehending the legislative process concerning financial matters in India.
